title: Menu Extraction Schema V3
description: Schema for menu extraction. This version separates category-level and item-level descriptive evidence into multiple natural-language fields so a downstream model can semantically distinguish sizes, options, toppings, pricing, and other rules. Markdown chunks may be jumbled, so rely on visual cues, layout, and semantic understanding more than markdown order when deciding what belongs together. Do not miss important information. Every descriptive field should be complete, customer-meaningful, and useful for later structuring, especially when the source text is terse, fragmented, or visually ambiguous.

global_hours.description: The global operating hours applying to the whole menu, if present, must be extracted here. Use this field only for operating hours that genuinely apply at the whole-menu level and not individual categories.

categories.description: Categories or sections in visual reading order. Do not create a shared section when the information applies to only one category; in that case, keep it inside that category's own descriptive fields. Do not create duplicate categories. If a category does not show its own pricing structure, it most likely depends on a shared section and should refer to that shared section unless pricing is truly absent from the menu.

category_name.description: Category or section heading exactly as printed on the menu. Never invent or paraphrase a category name.

category_ref.description: Normalized local reference for this category or section. This is used so other categories or shared sections can refer to it in structured form during downstream processing. Each category_ref must be unique within the menu. If two categories would otherwise produce the same reference, use numeric suffixes to deduplicate them.

category_role.description: Role of this category or section within the menu structure. Use `normal_category` for a regular category. Use one of the shared section roles only when the extracted section is actually a shared sizes, options, toppings, modifiers, or mixed shared section rather than a normal item category. A shared section should apply to multiple categories; if the information applies to only one category, keep it inside that category instead.

category_type.description: Standardized category bucket for downstream grouping and RMF report-category classification. Choose the best enum for this category based on the printed heading and item content.

category_description.description: Verbatim category description exactly as printed on the menu for this category or section. Preserve the printed wording as closely as possible. Leave empty if the category has no printed description. Do not paraphrase this field. If there is any other important category-level information, note, hour, disclaimer, included side, preparation note, or rule that does not fit naturally into the sizes, options, toppings, or pricing fields, extract that important information verbatim here as well.

category_hours.description: Verbatim operating-hours text that applies specifically to this individual category or section and not to the whole menu. Use this only for category-specific hours. Do not duplicate whole-menu or global hours here. Leave empty if this category has no specific hours.

category_sizes.description: Natural-language description of the sizes that apply to the whole category or shared section, not to one item only. Do not merely copy terse fragments or raw labels. Explain the size structure in the kind of natural language you would use to clearly explain it to a customer, while still preserving exact printed size labels and pricing details. Include quantity differences, pricing logic, and any ambiguity that matters for structuring. If the source is terse or fragmentary, explain what the text most likely means without inventing information.

category_options.description: Natural-language description of options, modifiers, substitutions, add-ons, crust choices, protein choices, sauce choices, or other selectable changes that apply to the whole category or shared section. Do not merely copy terse fragments or raw labels. Explain the options in the kind of natural language you would use to clearly explain them to a customer, while still preserving exact printed names, headings, min/max rules, implied choices, and any size-based option pricing if present.

category_toppings.description: Natural-language description of toppings that apply to the whole category or shared section. Do not merely copy terse fragments or raw lists. Explain the topping choices in the kind of natural language you would use to clearly explain them to a customer, while still preserving exact printed topping names and pricing details. Distinguish default toppings from available add-on toppings whenever the menu supports that distinction. Include pricing and half-topping information when present.

category_pricing.description: Natural-language description of category-level or shared pricing logic. Do not merely copy terse fragments or raw price strings. Explain the pricing in the kind of natural language you would use to clearly explain it to a customer, while still preserving exact prices, labels, and relationships. Include base prices, size prices, bundle prices, upcharges, included items, and any relationships between sizes, toppings, options, and final price. If the printed pricing is terse, fragmented, or visually hard to interpret, explain that clearly.

applies_to_category_refs.description: Structured references to the categories this section applies to when this category is acting as a shared sizes, options, toppings, modifiers, or mixed shared section. Populate this only when a shared section truly applies to multiple normal categories.

modifiables_defined_in_category_refs.description: Structured references to other categories or sections where shared sizes, options, toppings, pricing, or other shared descriptive evidence for this category are actually defined. Populate this when this normal category depends on separately extracted shared sections.

items.description: Items nested under this category, in visual order. Extract ALL items that belong under this category.

item_name.description: Name of the individual item as best understood from the menu. Preserve the full printed item name. Always include the item serial number, alphabetic label, or alphanumeric serial in the item name whenever it is present on the menu.

item_description.description: Verbatim item description exactly as printed on the menu for this individual item. Preserve the printed wording as closely as possible. Leave empty if the item has no printed description. Do not paraphrase this field.

item_sizes.description: Natural-language description of sizes that apply specifically to this individual item and not to the whole category. Be descriptive and complete. Include exact size labels, base-price relationships, and any ambiguity that matters for later structuring.

item_options.description: Natural-language description of options, modifiers, substitutions, add-ons, flavor choices, protein choices, sauce choices, crust choices, or other selectable changes that apply specifically to this item. Be descriptive and complete. Include implied options when supported by the menu and include size-based option pricing when present.

item_toppings.description: Natural-language description of toppings that apply specifically to this item. Be descriptive and complete. Distinguish default toppings from optional add-on toppings whenever possible. Include topping prices and half-topping information when present.

item_pricing.description: Natural-language description of all pricing that applies specifically to this item. Be descriptive and complete. Explain direct prices, size prices, included variants, add-on prices, option upcharges, and any special pricing logic. If the printed pricing is terse or visually ambiguous, explain that clearly.

item_rules_or_notes.description: Natural-language description of all remaining item-specific rules, notes, included sides, preparation details, warnings, or other important information that is not already captured in the other item-level descriptive fields. Be descriptive and complete.
